subject: Private deployment: evidence & license scope for MSA addendum
messages:
From: Matthew Carroll <matthew.carroll@avabridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: AvaBridge Legal <legal@avabridge.com>; procurement@avabridge.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: private deployment license scope + evidence for MSA addendum

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're starting final procurement work for our pilot (Order Form forthcoming) and need to align on two things before we can circulate to Finance and Security:

1) License & deployment rights for a private VPC/on-prem model install — specifically: is the intent-to-serve license a run-of-business license scoped to a single application instance, or do you offer site-wide operator rights that would allow our ops team to run multiple inference clusters? We need clear wording we can insert into our MSA addendum.

2) Audit/evidence pathway — our security team requires an audit bundle for on-prem deployments: operator-runner witnessability, snapshot proofs of access, and a 3rd-party-friendly method for key custody verification. We heard about an "escrow-lite" path in your docs; can you confirm what's included and what evidence Redwood can deliver vs. what AvaBridge must provide?

Timing: procurement wants the redlined MSA addendum and an evidence checklist by end of next week. Is that feasible from your side?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Matt Carroll
Head of IT Procurement
AvaBridge Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Carroll <matthew.carroll@avabridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment license scope + evidence for MSA addendum

Matt —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can deliver a scoped site license OR an instance-bound license depending on the commercial term you prefer; and we can support an "escrow-lite" evidence package that includes snapshots, operator witness, and an attestation report.

Plan: I've looped in Laura (legal) and Priyom (product/ops). Laura will propose MSA addendum language to make the license boundary explicit (site vs. instance). Priyom will confirm the operational artifacts we can produce and the expected lead time for a witnessed snapshot.

Two clarifying Qs for AvaBridge security so we can tailor the evidence:
- Do you require the snapshot to be taken by a Redwood operator onsite, or is a remote witnessed process (Redwood runs snapshot, AvaBridge witness via video + signed attestation) acceptable?
- For key custody, do you need an HSM-backed handback, or will a KMS-backed snapshot plus hashchain verification and witness attestation satisfy your auditors?

I've attached an initial RFI response that outlines the typical footprint and evidence items we can provide. We'll aim to get redlines to you within 48 hours; if procurement needs lawyers to talk matters through, propose times and we'll set up a call.

—Jonas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Initial_RFI_Response_AvaBridge.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment license scope + evidence for MSA addendum

Team —

Drafted a short addendum and a set of carve options. High-level recommendations below; attached is a tracked-change draft (Redlines_MSA_AvaBridge_20260530.docx). Please review for product feasibility.

Key legal positions:
- License scope: default to "instance-bound" (single deployment per Order Form) with an explicit option to convert to "site license" via an Order Form amendment and scaled pricing. This keeps commercial predictability while giving the customer a path to expand.
- Audit evidence: Redwood will provide
  * Snapshot proof: logical snapshot + hashchain and a witness attestation (remote or onsite)
  * Operator access: temporary console access windows for agreed audit sessions (timeboxed, logged)
  * Key custody: Redwood will not hand over private signing keys; instead we propose KMS-backed export of sealed artifacts and a notarized attestation by an independent witness.
- Escrow-lite: propose a clause referencing a third-party custodian or notary who can attest to snapshot integrity upon a defined trigger (bankruptcy / insolvency / protracted service failure). This is not a full software escrow but satisfies typical procurement ask.

Questions for Priyom: are the witness attestation and the timeboxed console access operationally realistic? If not, Laura's suggested fallback is to broaden the export + notarized attestation option.

I'll prepare the tracked-wording that we can send to AvaBridge legal. If they want on-site witness, we should flag travel/costs as an exhibit.

—Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redlines_MSA_AvaBridge_20260530.docx
From: Matthew Carroll <matthew.carroll@avabridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: AvaBridge Legal <legal@avabridge.com>; procurement@avabridge.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment license scope + evidence for MSA addendum

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what our security team expected. A few quick notes:

- Remote witnessed snapshot is acceptable provided we get a short video link + signed attestation and the hashchain value.
- The escrow-lite clause with a third-party notary is fine; please include a short exhibit estimating cost and expected timeline for an on-site witness (we may not need it, but need the option).
- Procurement confirms the deal id AVB-2026-0457; we will circulate your redlined MSA to our legal and aim to return counters within 5 business days.

Next steps: please upload the redline and evidence checklist to the HubSpot record and send a DocuSign packet when you're ready. If possible, include an itemized fee line for an on-site witness.
